 Advertisement From hot dogs to gelato: Here are the major recalls announced this week
 Advertisement Updated: 12:00 PM EDT Oct 23, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Brian Wiechert Digital Content Manager From hot dogs to gelato: Here are the major recalls announced this week
 Updated: 12:00 PM EDT Oct 23, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Brian Wiechert Digital Content Manager Consumers faced a wide range of recalls last week, spanning food, household products, medications and vehicles. 
 Among the bigger recalls last week were a massive meat recall from Kayem Foods and fire-risk recalls involving Toyota and Hyundai vehicles. 
 Advertisement Related video above | Check your fridge: Recalled foods could already be in your home 
 Food alerts also covered items such as gelato, smoked salmon and cheddar cheese, while several children’s products raised concerns about button batteries or safe sleep. Toothpaste, pet medications and patio heaters rounded out a varied week for recalls.
 Below is a breakdown of the major recalls issued over the past two weeks. 
 FOOD ITEMS 
 Dried beans. Natural Grocers recalled certain 2-pound bags of its organic mung beans after customers reported sharp glass fragments. The affected lots were shipped to stores in 23 states beginning in June 2026. Click here to view the full recall .
 Ready-to-eat meat and poultry. Kayem Foods recalled about 1.58 million pounds of products, including hot dogs, bacon, deli meat and bratwursts, because they may have been held at unsafe temperatures. Click here to view the full recall .
 Gelato. Lidl US recalled one lot of Gelatelli Coffee & Vanilla Gelato after routine testing found possible Listeria contamination. The affected product was sold in Lidl stores in several states, including Georgia and South Carolina. Click here to view the full recall .
 Cold-smoked salmon. Krasnyi Oktyabr recalled Starfish Seafood Premium Cold Smoked Norwegian Salmon because it may be contaminated with Listeria. The 8-ounce product was distributed in several states, including Georgia. Click here to view the full recall .
 Raw cheddar cheese. Family Farmstead Dairy recalled a specific lot of its raw mild cheddar cheese because it may be contaminated with E. coli. The affected cheese was distributed to retailers in several states, and may have reached others through downstream distributors. Click here to view the full recall .
 Hoagie rolls. WinCo Foods recalled certain hoagie rolls because their labels did not disclose sesame, which may trigger a serious or life-threatening reaction in people with a sesame allergy. The rolls were sold at WinCo stores in California, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Oregon, Utah and Washington. Click here to view the full recall .
 Raw oysters. Little Wicomico Oyster Company recalled oysters harvested from Virginia’s Little Wicomico River from Sept. 18 through Oct. 8, 2026, because they may be contaminated with Salmonella. The oysters were distributed to restaurants and retailers in multiple states, including Georgia. Click here to view the full recall . 
 HOUSEHOLD GOODS
 Papablic infant swings. The recalled Archie baby swings pose a suffocation risk if used for infant sleep because their incline exceeds the limit allowed for infant sleep products. Click here to view the full recall .
 LED finger-light toys. BAMAMON projecting finger lights contain button batteries in compartments children can access, posing a risk of serious injury or death if a battery is swallowed. Click here to view the full recall .
 Light-up princess costumes. CIYTI costumes were recalled because children can access the button batteries, creating a serious ingestion hazard. Click here to view the full recall .
 Convertible high chairs. Costway recalled high chairs that convert into a table and chair set because they pose entrapment and fall hazards and violate the mandatory high-chair standard. Click here to view the full recall .
 Gas patio heaters. VQQQ patio heaters were recalled because they pose fire and burn hazards that could cause serious injury or death. Click here to view the full recall .
 Commercial outdoor lights. Certain Lithonia Lighting RSX luminaires may detach from their adjustable tilt arms if a mounting joint fails, creating an impact hazard. Click here to view the full recall .
 MEDICATIONS
 Toothpaste products. More than 4.3 million tubes of Brush Buddies, evo and ARU toothpaste were recalled over manufacturing practice deviations. The affected products include children’s character-themed and flavored toothpastes, as well as adult products. Click here to view the full recall . 
 Compounded pet medications. Wedgewood Pharmacy recalled certain compounded veterinary medications because unreliable testing data could mean some products are too weak or too strong, potentially causing ineffective treatment or overdose. Click here to view the full recall .
 Amazon-branded acetaminophen. Certain Amazon Basic Care Extra Strength acetaminophen caplets were recalled after reports that tablets had become discolored. Click here to view the full recall .
 VEHICLES
 Toyota vehicles. Toyota recalled certain vehicles after a fuel tube defect was found that could cause a fuel leak and increase the risk of fire. Click here to view the full recall . 
 Hyundai and Genesis vehicles. The recall covers certain Genesis and Genesis G80 vehicles whose power seat motors could overheat if a control switch sticks, creating a fire risk. Click here to view the full recall .
